headline: Andy Burnham says rejoining the EU among all ‘the options’ being considered – UK politics live

members.title: Andy Burnham says rejoining the EU among all ‘the options’ being considered – UK politics live
members.lead: The PM says all ‘the options’ being considered and calls for an open debate about the UK’s future relationship with Europe Burnham: UK could ‘go all the way’ by rejoining EU Burnham wants to review the UK’s relationship with the EU. What are the options? Key takeaways from Andy Burnham’s conference speech Andy Burnham has suggested that it would not be legitimate for a party to form a majority government with less than 30% of the vote. In his Today interview, asked why he wanted electoral reform and a move towards proportional representation, Burnham replied: I found it better being elected under a different system as mayor of Greater Manchester, where people had one or two, they could put that on the ballot paper. Because you had a reason to stop on every doorstep and chat to people who might not always support your party and try and get their second preference. No, it could happen with any political party. It’s whether that would be a legitimate government. I think you’ve got it completely wrong really, if you don’t mind me saying, to put it like that, because I have put out … a vision for a national care service. There are pensioners out there who watch your programme who are paying for care costs from their basic state pension. Now, is that right or fair? Continue reading...

members.title: Andy Burnham: UK could ‘go all the way’ by rejoining EU
members.lead: PM says he is looking at all options and ministers will examine ‘what is doable’ and the ‘pros and cons’ UK politics live – latest updates Andy Burnham has opened the door to the UK rejoining the EU, saying Britain could “go all the way”, as he prepares to reconsider Labour’s post-Brexit red lines. The prime minister used a series of interviews after his emotional Labour conference speech to spell out how wide-ranging his consideration of Britain’s future with Brussels could be because Brexit had caused “more harm than good”.
